Job Scams

By: Sipha Kema | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Job hunting in South Africa has now become an extreme sport for many desperate job seekers...

Unique Selling Point:
With the high unemployment rate and scarcity of jobs in South Africa, job scams have evolved - job seekers are now risking their lives.
Job hunting in South Africa is life threatening.

While many stories have been done on job scams, we will show it as how it's changed with times and aiding in human trafficking in SA.

Summary:
With a thin job market and the continuously growing unemployment rate, South Africans have become increasingly desperate to earn a living. This is something criminals have become aware of, and taken advantage of. With the changing times, so have scams - these scammers have now become dangerous yet South Africans still fall prey to this hustle.

We start in the Eastern Cape in Matatiele with Sisters Nthabiseng and Refiloe Tibane have found themselves join the many victims conned by Andisiwe Mngenela in Matatiele.

Andisiwe Mngenela is known to promise desperate unemployed women jobs within the municipality at Matatiele Local Municipality and Alfred Nzo District Municipality , all the job seeker has to do is pay a “refundable” amount of R3500 to ensure the job is theirs. Unfortunately, all the women who have been promised work have never seen a job contract or gotten their money back.

The two Tibane sisters were conned to believe there are vacancies open at the district municipality, they're urgently were looking employees to fill the mayoral initiative to alleviate unemployment especially in Matatiele and sorroundings. Andisiwe told the sisters that they needed to pay the amount of R3000 which will be paid back by the mayor because there were allegation that there was money missing so the mayor wanted to sort out that issue. Out of desperation and assurance that money will be paid back, the money was then deposited to her account. (proof of deposit receipts with Andisiwe Mngenela account number)

In such a small town, this lady has become quite the fugitive, making it hard for people to get their money back. Andisiwe is also known to hang around unsavoury characters whom many of her victims fear. As a result some are scared to talk.

In Johannesburg we move to Lerato Ralele who escaped an attempted kidnapping whilst at a bogus job interview in Johannesburg CBD. Lerato will detail how she applied for the job and the process leading up to her ïnterview". She will then talk to us about what exactly happened at the interview. How did they attempt to kidnap her and how did she escape.

A21 an international NGO fighting against human trafficking will also tell us their first hand experience of dealing with survivors who fell victim to job scams. - A21 also helps counsel victims who survived human trafficking as a result of bogus jobs.

Further information:
We setup a bait for Andisiwe as she’s still scamming and operating. unfortunately she has gone MIA, someone gave her a tipoff after I had started communicating with her. We will start with confronting Andisiwe, we have traced her to her hiding spot. She is our villian in the story. We will pop up at her hiding spot.

We will also talk to the Matatiele Local Municipality and find out how Andisiwe is using her cousin (the mayor's) name to continue with her scams after people came to the municipality for fake interviews.

Press Release:


It’s a startling statistic: almost 33 percent of people living in South Africa are unemployed, many of them unemployable. It’s fertile ground for scammers who prey on desperate jobseekers. In Matatiele, in the Eastern Cape, a well-connected and widely known woman has become notorious for using her ties to a local mayor to dupe desperate jobseekers. Offering work at the municipality, she charges a small fee for her services but never delivers. And she’s not alone. In Gauteng, a rogue recruitment agency is one of several using the promise of jobs to defraud the desperate and already chronically poor. Carte Blanche investigates.

0000-00-00 Press Release: It’s a startling statistic: almost 33 percent of people living in South Africa are unemployed, many of them unemployable. It’s fertile ground for scammers who prey on desperate jobseekers. In Matatiele, in the Eastern Cape, a well-connected and widely known woman has become notorious for using her ties to a local mayor to dupe desperate jobseekers. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Job hunting in South Africa has now become an extreme sport for many desperate job seekers...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: With the high unemployment rate and scarcity of jobs in South Africa, job scams have evolved - job seekers are now risking their lives. Job hunting in South Africa is life threatening. While many stories have been done on job scams, we will show it as how it's changed with times and aiding in human trafficking in SA.
metadata.Summary: With a thin job market and the continuously growing unemployment rate, South Africans have become increasingly desperate to earn a living. This is something criminals have become aware of, and taken advantage of. With the changing times, so have scams - these scammers have now become dangerous yet South Africans still fall prey to this hustle. We start in the Eastern Cape in Matatiele with Sisters Nthabiseng and Refiloe Tibane have found themselves join the many victims conned by Andisiwe Mngenela in Matatiele. Andisiwe Mngenela is known to promise desperate unemployed women jobs within the municipality at Matatiele Local Municipality and Alfred Nzo District Municipality , all the job seeker has to do is pay a “refundable” amount of R3500 to ensure the job is theirs. Unfortunately, all the women who have been promised work have never seen a job contract or gotten their money back. The two Tibane sisters were conned to believe there are vacancies open at the district municipality, they're urgently were looking employees to fill the mayoral initiative to alleviate unemployment especially in Matatiele and sorroundings. Andisiwe told the sisters that they needed to pay the amount of R3000 which will be paid back by the mayor because there were allegation that there was money missing so the mayor wanted to sort out that issue. Out of desperation and assurance that money will be paid back, the money was then deposited to her account. (proof of deposit receipts with Andisiwe Mngenela account number) In such a small town, this lady has become quite the fugitive, making it hard for people to get their money back. Andisiwe is also known to hang around unsavoury characters whom many of her victims fear. As a result some are scared to talk. In Johannesburg we move to Lerato Ralele who escaped an attempted kidnapping whilst at a bogus job interview in Johannesburg CBD. Lerato will detail how she applied for the job and the process leading up to her ïnterview". She will then talk to us about what exactly happened at the interview. How did they attempt to kidnap her and how did she escape. A21 an international NGO fighting against human trafficking will also tell us their first hand experience of dealing with survivors who fell victim to job scams. - A21 also helps counsel victims who survived human trafficking as a result of bogus jobs.
